svg.title: Feedback types, generalized failure modes and enforced prevention
svg.desc: Six feedback types feed evidence-based analysis. Agents generalize the cause and choose shared instructions, skills, shared tools and code, checks and gates, architecture and plans, or the failure-pattern checklist. General feedback and skill-use feedback have separate evidence paths. Explicit enforcement proof and later recurrence reports close the loop. A missing-tooltip example illustrates the difference between a local repair and generalized prevention; its cause remains to be verified. Current reports now feed the existing failure-pattern reviewer alongside the legacy register.
svg.text: Feedback → generalized failure modes → enforced prevention
The visible problem is the starting point. Preventing the same kind of failure is the outcome.
The verified cause decides what changes; a feedback type does not have one fixed destination.

g.text: A rule, tool or hook obstructed work.
A question, a trial and its result.
A correction or a standing rule.
Where a skill helped or failed.
First five: shared log + weekly review
Skill use: skill log + skill review
Keep quotes, results and evidence links
For failures: name the root cause.
Add a check or structural prevention
Fix the mechanism at its source
Redesign a cause that needs wider work
Name failure families; guide future audits

svg.text: Agent reads and tests the evidence
Agent chooses one or more targets
Solid: collection / review paths. Dashed: agent analysis and applied changes.

g.text: After enforcement: does the same failure recur?
Central-loop fixes: later reports + enforcement proof → daily watcher → verified repeat reopens the task.

svg.text: Illustrative failure mode; the actual cause must be verified.

g.text: Default review: current feedback and legacy entries feed the same failure-pattern reviewer.

svg.text: Also feeds: your impact-ranked problem view and high-impact alerts.
Record forms: observation = what happened; claim = what it means; action = what was tried.
Your explicit directions authorize changes. Independent-support checks apply to loop-derived fixes. • 8 October 2026
